newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch shares closed a thin day's range-bound trading marginally up on Friday, cheered by opening gains on Wall Street in the wake of long-awaited U.S. employment figures.
The AEX index of Dutch blue chips ended 0.31 points higher at 553.39, after having spent most of the day hovering around support at 550.
Dealers said that in the absence of any Dutch corporate earnings figures to give the market direction the day's trade had been dominated by the U.S. data, released at 1230 GMT.
U.S. payrolls came in 6,000 higher than expected at 250,000.
U.S. August unemployment was also lower than expected, at 5.1 percent.

An initial flurry of activity after the U.S. numbers sent Dutch shares spiralling lower to an intra-day nadir of 546.30, but they rallied almost immediately in line with bunds and T-bonds, which had also plummeted at first.
Commenting on the figures, U.S. Labour secretary Robert Reich said the strength of the figures had not translated into wage-push inflation.
Stronger bonds and a higher opening on Wall Street also gave support late in the session.
Down most of the day, index-heavy financials also ended the session narrowly up, with banks ING and ABN AMRO both putting on 10 guilder cents to 51.60 and 89.60 respectively.

KLM Royal Dutch Airlines bucked the day's downtrend thanks to a higher load factor in August. After trading up 0.20 at 45.40 most of the day in a falling market it followed the late surge to end 0.50 guilders higher at 45.70.

Supermarket giant Ahold built on Thursday's slim gains, adding 0.40 to 93.70. Dealers said second-quarter profit figures at the top end of analysts' forecasts had held no surprises for the market. "The good news was already there," one said.
